required_knowns.claim: The public MCP schema exposes name, file, line, language and edge_kind. The handler requires a supplied file to be a nonempty string and a supplied line to be a positive u32 accompanied by file. It checks index freshness before forwarding the arguments to queries::callees.

Candidate selection starts with exact-name definitions, optionally filtered by language. name_collision counts these definitions before file/line selectors. File and declaration-start line are equality filters, not substring or containing-range searches. Selectors must leave exactly one definition; file alone need not distinguish declarations within one file.

Zero remaining candidates produces not_found, one produces matched, and several produce ambiguous. Only the unique matched definition supplies an ID for the outgoing-edge query. Ambiguous/not_found return no selected definition and no callees; matched can also have an empty callee list. Ambiguity and not_found are successful query-layer outcomes and can be returned with isError=false when the response fits MCP result limits. An oversized payload or envelope instead produces a tool error. isError=false and count=0 alone do not establish that a definition has no dependencies.

For the selected source definition, Store::callees_of returns DISTINCT pairs of stored to_name and edge line, filtered by from_id and edge kind, with calls as the default. It does not join target definitions or use to_id, to_type or target_kind to identify an outgoing target. The returned line is edges.line, not a target declaration line, and count measures returned name/line pairs rather than resolved target definitions or runtime invocations.

Selecting one source definition does not upgrade target resolution. edge_precision is derived from that definition's file extension; for .rs it reports medium confidence, syntactic extraction and target_resolution=name_based_candidates. The declared limitations include unresolved trait-object/function-pointer dispatch and unexpanded macros. calls and references are separate filters, references do not prove invocation, and empty results do not prove complete dependency absence.

expected_unknowns: Without concrete indexed declarations and edges, the actual candidates, selected definition and outgoing entries for a particular request remain unknown.
This result does not establish which implementation executes at runtime or complete dependency coverage. The extraction implementations and compiler/runtime evidence are outside the source allowlist.
No execution was performed. The presence of regression tests in these files does not establish their runtime outcome, CI status or installed-binary behavior.
materially_false_claims: The tool silently selects the first same-named declaration or merges their outgoing edges when the remaining candidates are ambiguous.
A file selector always resolves ambiguity, or line selects any declaration whose body contains that line.
name_collision counts outgoing targets or necessarily becomes one after a successful file/line selection.
An ambiguous response necessarily has isError=true, or count=0 proves that the requested definition has no dependencies.
Selecting the source definition also selects the exact definitions of all outgoing targets.
callees[].line identifies the target declaration, or count is the number of resolved target definitions.
resolution=syntactic or match_status=matched establishes compiler/type resolution.
The default calls filter includes references, or a references edge proves invocation.
This research run executed runtime tests or graph queries, or confirmed CI or installed-binary behavior.
reviewer_notes: A separate read-only agent reviewed the claims and anchors against the exact pinned Git objects; the coordinator independently checked the MCP, query and storage boundaries. This is agent source review, not runtime evidence, human sign-off or a model-quality measurement.
The public surface in scope is MCP. CLI dispatch, explain, incoming callers, transitive impact and optional SCIP resolution are not required conclusions.
The key distinguishes selecting the source declaration from resolving outgoing targets. Store::callees_of does not apply the compatibility predicates used by other graph queries.
The argument claim describes the advertised schema and the handler's explicit file/line checks; it does not claim that every schema constraint is generically enforced at runtime.
A supplied file and start line can still leave several candidates if multiple declarations share both values. The implementation then remains ambiguous.
A source-grounded description of a regression test's assertions is valid evidence of the test contract; it must not be described as an observed passing test.
A second independent source review identified the MCP result-size boundary. Query success must not be generalized into unconditional MCP delivery success; both payload and full envelope are bounded.
